options.C: Ask the patient to pay for a replacement needle
options.D: Perform a thorough search of the room and take an X-ray

explanation: Spot on! A missing needle means a full search of the room and an X-ray to confirm where it went. [learn more](GNS123_U5_T8#GNS123_U5_T8_h5)

question: What is the normal resting breathing rate for a healthy adult?

options.A: 30 to 40 breaths per minute
options.B: 8 to 12 breaths per minute
options.C: 20 to 30 breaths per minute
options.D: 12 to 20 breaths per minute

explanation: Healthy adults take between 12 and 20 breaths every minute while resting. Easy to remember for your exams! [learn more](GNS112_U6_T2#GNS112_U6_T2_h4)

question: Which portable device does a patient wear to continuously send heart rhythm data to the nurse's station?

options.A: A standard mercury sphygmomanometer
options.B: A handheld blood glucose meter
options.C: A telemetry transmitter
options.D: A basic digital thermometer

explanation: Telemetry packs are worn by the patient to wirelessly beam their ECG rhythm straight to the central monitor. Very handy for cardiac patients!

question: What is the primary goal of teaching oncology patients about emergency warning signs?

options.A: To ensure they seek help quickly before symptoms become life-threatening
options.B: To prevent them from ever experiencing another tumor recurrence
options.C: To train them to manage medical emergencies at home without calling a doctor
options.D: To reduce the financial cost of hospital stays

explanation: Early reporting of red-flag symptoms allows healthcare teams to intervene swiftly before minor issues become full-blown emergencies. [learn more](GNS321_U1_T13#GNS321_U1_T13_h7)

question: How can an unsterile instrument used during an abortion lead to septic shock?

options.A: By introducing bacteria that multiply and spread into the bloodstream
options.B: By causing an immediate allergic reaction inside the womb
options.C: By cutting off oxygen to the major abdominal organs
options.D: By causing a sudden drop in blood pressure purely from pain

explanation: Unclean tools carry germs straight into the womb, causing a severe infection that can enter the bloodstream and trigger shock. You're mastering the basics of sepsis!

question: A mum receiving oxytocin gets intensely distressed, and the monitor shows late decelerations. What is your best immediate action?

options.A: Administer an oral stimulant medication
options.B: Increase the oxytocin drip rate to speed up delivery
options.C: Stop the oxytocin infusion immediately
options.D: Encourage the patient to push harder right away

explanation: Stopping the oxytocin stops the strong contractions from straining the uterus further, helping oxygen flow back to the baby.

question: Which of these is a natural, drug-free way to help a mum cope with labour pain?

options.A: Epidural anesthesia block
options.B: Intravenous opioid administration
options.C: Continuous back rubs and hydrotherapy
options.D: General surgical anesthesia

explanation: Massages, warm water (hydrotherapy), and breathing exercises work wonders for natural pain relief without medications.

question: Who usually passes down nutritional taboos in traditional communities?

options.A: Modern clinical dietitians and nurses
options.B: Community elders and cultural leaders
options.C: Local government agricultural officers
options.D: International health organization workers

explanation: Generational beliefs and food rules are typically preserved and taught by the older members and leaders of the community.

question: What makes the Oral Polio Vaccine (OPV) so great for massive community campaigns?

options.A: It is given through an injection that leaves a lasting scar
options.B: It contains live bacteria that cure existing paralysis
options.C: It does not require any temperature control or refrigeration
options.D: It is simple to administer and builds good gut immunity

explanation: Brilliant! Drops are easy to give without needing injection pros, and they build strong defense right where the virus enters—the gut.

question: Which group is usually eligible for DRF exemptions in our hospitals?

options.A: Elected political office holders
options.B: Employed corporate executives
options.C: Wealthy private business owners
options.D: Indigent elderly patients without support

explanation: Older adults who lack pensions or family financial backup are standard beneficiaries of these hospital welfare safety nets.

question: Why must you stay right by the patient during the first 15 minutes of a blood transfusion?

options.A: Hospital accreditation rules require physical presence to document vital signs
options.B: Most severe, life-threatening transfusion reactions occur during this initial window
options.C: Patients often feel lonely and anxious when receiving intravenous fluids
options.D: Pumps automatically lock out nurse access after fifteen minutes of running

explanation: Most bad reactions happen right at the beginning when the blood first hits circulation. Staying close lets you catch it instantly!

question: Besides blood-borne viruses, what other common infection can result from using non-sterile injection equipment?

options.A: Bacterial infections causing abscesses and sepsis
options.B: Fungal infections affecting the respiratory tract
options.C: Parasitic infections residing in the bloodstream
options.D: Genetic disorders altering red blood cells

explanation: Unsterile equipment introduces bacteria straight into tissues, which can lead to painful local abscesses or severe blood infections like sepsis.

question: What is the main goal of hygiene care for older school-age children compared to babies?

options.A: Forcing the child to bathe without any adult assistance whatsoever
options.B: Teaching the child how to operate heavy plumbing valves
options.C: Encouraging safe self-care and independence under supervision
options.D: Eliminating the need for soap entirely

explanation: You got it! School-age kids are ready to learn good hygiene habits themselves while we supervise to make sure they stay safe.

question: A patient presents to the clinic complaining of bleeding after sexual intercourse and a foul-smelling vaginal discharge. What is the most appropriate initial nursing action?

options.A: Advise her to start taking heavy doses of oral iron supplements immediately
options.B: Instruct her to apply medicated vaginal creams every night for a month
options.C: Reassure her that this is a normal part of aging and send her home
options.D: Perform a detailed health history and facilitate a pelvic examination by the doctor

explanation: Post-coital bleeding requires prompt clinical investigation and visualization of the cervix to rule out malignancy. [learn more](GNS216_U5_T18#GNS216_U5_T18_h4)

question: Why is it important to use the correct blood pressure cuff size?

options.A: It prevents the patient from feeling any pressure at all
options.B: An incorrect size leads to inaccurate blood pressure readings
options.C: Hospital regulations require matching cuffs to patient age only
options.D: Small cuffs are easier to wrap around the arm quickly

explanation: A cuff that is too small gives a falsely high reading, while one that is too large gives a falsely low reading. [learn more](GNS112_U6_T1#GNS112_U6_T1_h5)

question: Where are the majority of nephrons primarily located within the kidney tissue?

options.A: In the renal capsule
options.B: In the renal cortex
options.C: In the renal medulla
options.D: In the renal pelvis

explanation: Most nephrons are situated in the outer layer of the kidney known as the cortex, while only a small portion extends deep into the medulla. [learn more](GNS121_U2_T5#GNS121_U2_T5_h1)

question: A patient with post-traumatic stress disorder startles violently at a sudden loud noise. Which limbic structure is most likely driving this hyperactive reaction?

options.A: The cerebellum
options.B: The occipital lobe
options.C: The amygdala
options.D: The hippocampus

explanation: An overactive amygdala is responsible for the exaggerated fear and startle responses seen in conditions like PTSD. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T13#GNS211_U3_T13_h6)

question: Which strategy works best when designing health messages for communities with low literacy levels?

options.A: Using pictorial guides, local radio jingles, and interactive drama performances
options.B: Relying entirely on detailed medical charts during community lectures
options.C: Distributing dense academic textbooks written in English about chronic diseases
options.D: Requiring all participants to read online health blogs before clinic visits

explanation: Wonderful! Pictures, local drama, and radio bypass reading barriers, making health education fun and easy for everyone to understand.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical focus of cognitive behavioral therapy (CBT) for sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Reframing unhelpful beliefs regarding sexuality
options.B: Reducing anxiety related to sexual performance
options.C: Surgical reconstruction of the pelvic floor muscles
options.D: Challenging negative thoughts about body image

explanation: Spot on! CBT is all about thoughts, feelings, and behaviors—surgeries are definitely left for surgical specialists!

question: Which immune cells are on the front lines, patrolling tissues to destroy abnormal cells?

options.A: Albumin and globulin proteins
options.B: Eosinophils and basophils
options.C: Red blood cells and platelets
options.D: T-cells and natural killer cells

explanation: You got it! T-cells and natural killer (NK) cells are the heavy lifters of the immune system, constantly hunting down and destroying abnormal or infected cells.

question: A nurse is caring for an adult with diabetes who works on a farm. What is the most important health risk to keep an eye on?

options.A: Absence of any need for routine immunization boosters
options.B: Complete resistance to vector-borne diseases
options.C: Increased susceptibility to infections due to chronic illness
options.D: Immediate lifelong immunity acquired from farm work

explanation: Chronic illnesses like diabetes can slow down healing and weaken the immune response, meaning this patient catches infections much more easily.

question: Which cells in the pancreas make insulin?

options.A: Beta cells
options.B: Acinar cells
options.C: Delta cells
options.D: Alpha cells

explanation: Spot on! Beta cells in the pancreas are the ones responsible for producing insulin to bring your blood sugar down.

question: At what specific location do nerve fibers from the inside of each retina cross to the other side?

options.A: Occipital lobe
options.B: Ciliary body
options.C: Optic disc
options.D: Optic chiasm

explanation: The optic chiasm is the X-shaped structure where partial crossover of visual nerve fibers occurs. [learn more](GNS211_U4_T1#GNS211_U4_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary difference between hypovolemic shock and cardiogenic shock?

options.A: Cardiogenic shock is caused by severe allergic reactions
options.B: Hypovolemic shock is caused by a blocked pulmonary artery
options.C: Cardiogenic shock involves heart pump failure, while hypovolemic shock involves fluid loss
options.D: Hypovolemic shock always features a very slow heart rate

explanation: In cardiogenic shock, blood volume is normal, but the heart muscle is too weak to pump it; in hypovolemic shock, the pump is fine, but volume is missing. [learn more](GNS123_U3_T5#GNS123_U3_T5_h4)

question: A patient with Type AB-positive blood needs emergency red blood cells and none of their exact type is available. Which blood type can they safely receive?

options.A: Any blood type
options.B: Only Type O-negative
options.C: Only Type A-positive
options.D: Only Type AB-positive

explanation: Type AB-positive individuals are universal recipients for red blood cells because their blood does not contain antibodies against A, B, or Rh antigens. [learn more](GNS111_U2_T2#GNS111_U2_T2_h5)

question: Why is a CT scan particularly useful for musculoskeletal disorders?

options.A: It clearly reveals complex fractures and deep bone issues.
options.B: It safely treats severe joint inflammation without surgery.
options.C: It provides real-time video of moving muscle fibers.
options.D: It completely replaces the need for physical assessments.

explanation: The layered, cross-sectional imaging of a CT scan allows healthcare providers to see intricate bone structures and hidden fractures that regular x-rays often miss. [learn more](GNS222_U1_T6#GNS222_U1_T6_h1)

question: What level of technique is normally used when changing chronic wound dressings at home?

options.A: Clean technique
options.B: Surgical sterility
options.C: Chemical disinfection only
options.D: Complete germ-free isolation

explanation: For routine home care, clean technique is the standard! It relies on solid hand hygiene and clean tools rather than trying to keep things operating-room sterile.

question: A patient keeps asking you to repeat yourself and turns one ear toward you when you speak. What is your best next nursing action?

options.A: Document that the patient has complete and permanent sensorineural deafness
options.B: Disregard the observation as a normal sign of aging requiring no action
options.C: Perform a focused auditory assessment and check for cerumen impaction
options.D: Refer the patient immediately for urgent visual acuity testing

explanation: Always start with simple nursing assessments first! Looking for a simple wax buildup (cerumen impaction) or checking hearing function is a great practical step before jumping to major conclusions.

question: If an expectant mother reports a sudden decrease in fetal movement, what should you suspect first?

options.A: The fetus has dropped into the pelvic cavity
options.B: The mother is simply too busy to notice kicks
options.C: Normal sleeping patterns of a full-term baby
options.D: Potential fetal distress or oxygen deprivation

explanation: Always take a drop in baby kicks seriously! It can be a vital warning sign that the baby is under distress and needs an urgent check-up.

question: Which oxygen delivery device provides the most precise and controlled oxygen concentration?

options.A: Non-rebreather mask
options.B: Standard nasal cannula
options.C: Simple face mask
options.D: Venturi mask

explanation: The Venturi mask uses interchangeable adapters to mix exact amounts of room air with oxygen, delivering a very specific percentage of gas. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h3)

question: Which finding in a new mother's lochia (postnatal discharge) should worry you the most?

options.A: A foul or offensive odor coming from the discharge
options.B: A slight increase in flow when the mother stands up
options.C: Small dark clots passed during the first three days
options.D: A gradual fading from red to pink over two weeks

explanation: Lochia naturally changes color and has a normal earthy smell, but a foul odor is a major sign of a uterine infection (endometritis) that needs quick treatment.

question: What is true about getting valid informed consent from a patient?

options.A: It is only necessary if the research involves major surgical procedures
options.B: It transfers the ownership of the patient's medical records to the researcher
options.C: It involves clear communication and genuine voluntary agreement, not just a signature
options.D: It can be waived by the nurse if the patient looks too tired to read

explanation: You got it! Consent isn't just about ticking a box or signing a paper—it's an ongoing conversation where the patient truly understands and freely agrees to take part.

question: What is the main job of normal lymphocytes in our body?

options.A: Fighting off infections and foreign invaders
options.B: Producing red blood cells in the bone marrow
options.C: Clotting blood to prevent bleeding
options.D: Carrying oxygen to body tissues

explanation: Think of lymphocytes as part of your body's security team! They are white blood cells that protect you against bacteria, viruses, and other germs.

question: When does diarrhoea officially change from being acute to chronic based on how long it lasts?

options.A: Chronic diarrhoea lasts longer than four weeks
options.B: Chronic diarrhoea lasts strictly seven to ten days
options.C: Chronic diarrhoea lasts less than forty-eight hours
options.D: Chronic diarrhoea lasts between three and five days

explanation: Think of it this way: short-term (acute) bugs clear up fast, but if diarrhoea hangs around for longer than four weeks, it's classed as chronic and needs a deeper look.

question: Once an expectorant thins out the respiratory mucus, what helps sweep it up toward the throat?

options.A: They absorb the excess fluid so the lungs stay completely dry
options.B: They dissolve the chemical bonds holding the phlegm together
options.C: They sweep the loosened mucus upward toward the throat
options.D: They produce more thick mucus to trap remaining dust particles

explanation: Meet the cilia—tiny hair-like structures in your airways that wave together like a stadium crowd to push that loosened mucus right up and out!

question: Why is learning about infectious agents so important for a community health nurse?

options.A: To diagnose rare genetic disorders in newborns
options.B: To prevent widespread disease outbreaks in populations
options.C: To replace the need for environmental sanitation workers
options.D: To manufacture antibiotics in local health centers

explanation: Spot on! When you understand how these tiny germs behave, you can help protect your entire community from getting sick. Great nursing insight!

question: Which hospital department usually conducts the financial check for an exemption request?

options.A: The main hospital kitchen
options.B: The hospital security department
options.C: The internal audit department
options.D: The social welfare unit

explanation: Social workers are specially trained to assess a patient's financial background and verify hardship before approving welfare waivers.

question: Roughly what happens to the size of an infant's brain during their very first year of life?

options.A: It stays the same
options.B: It cuts in half
options.C: It triples
options.D: It doubles

explanation: Amazing! Babies do a lot of growing; their brain volume actually triples in just that first year alone.

question: How can severe, untreated hyperemesis gravidarum impact the developing fetus?

options.A: It stops the umbilical cord from growing longer
options.B: It can lead to low birth weight or preterm delivery
options.C: It causes permanent skeletal bone deformities
options.D: It accelerates brain development too rapidly

explanation: When the mother cannot keep food down and loses significant weight, the baby may not get enough nutrients, raising the risk of low birth weight. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T012#GNS226_U2_T012_h6)

question: Why is water so crucial for chemical processes inside the body?

options.A: It is converted directly into stored body fat for warmth
options.B: It acts as a fluid medium for chemical reactions and transport
options.C: It slows down digestion so food stays in the stomach longer
options.D: It provides the primary source of daily dietary calories

explanation: Water is the ultimate carrier fluid. It provides the watery environment needed for chemical reactions and moves nutrients and waste all around the body.

question: An elderly patient with less muscle and more body fat takes a water-soluble drug. What is the likely result?

options.A: The drug spreads out forever and disappears
options.B: The drug instantly turns into a fat-soluble chemical
options.C: The drug fails to enter the bloodstream at all
options.D: The drug concentrates in a smaller fluid volume, leading to higher blood levels

explanation: Water-soluble drugs dissolve in body water. Since older adults usually have less total body water, a standard dose will be much more concentrated!

question: What is the main reason for 'physiological haemodilution' in pregnant women?

options.A: The bone marrow fails to produce any new blood cells
options.B: Red blood cells are actively destroyed by the maternal immune system
options.C: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell mass
options.D: Iron absorption in the small intestine drops to zero

explanation: Think of it like adding more water to juice—the fluid volume increases much faster than the red blood cells, making the blood appear 'thinned out' on lab tests. Completely normal and expected in pregnancy!

question: Which vaccine directly helps prevent a leading cause of childhood diarrhoea?

options.A: Tetanus toxoid vaccine
options.B: Hepatitis B vaccine
options.C: BCG tuberculosis vaccine
options.D: Rotavirus vaccine

explanation: Prevention is key! The rotavirus vaccine protects little ones from the most common viral bug that causes severe, dehydrating tummy bugs.

question: What type of medication is given to the scalp right before placing traction pins?

options.A: Topical antibiotic cream
options.B: Intravenous general anesthetic
options.C: Oral muscle relaxant
options.D: Local anesthetic

explanation: A local anesthetic is injected right where the pins will go so the patient stays completely numb and comfortable.

question: Which of these is a NORMAL finding and NOT a danger sign for a new mother?

options.A: Soaking through two large sanitary pads in one hour
options.B: A high fever with chills
options.C: Mild tiredness after caring for the baby at night
options.D: Sudden severe chest pain and trouble breathing

explanation: Every new mum is tired! But heavy bleeding, chest pain, and high fever are urgent warning signs that need immediate attention.

question: Which of the following is NOT a major challenge faced by public health nurses in many parts of Nigeria?

options.A: Excessive availability of ultra-modern robotic surgery equipment
options.B: Navigating cultural barriers and vaccine hesitancy in communities
options.C: Funding shortages affecting routine immunization supplies
options.D: Infrastructural deficits and poor road networks in remote areas

explanation: Robotic surgery equipment is found in advanced tertiary centers, not primary health care settings, making it an incorrect challenge for public health nurses. [learn more](GNS225_U1_T6#GNS225_U1_T6_h7)

question: Which lifestyle habit directly damages blood vessels and is a major cause of sexual dysfunction?

options.A: Cigarette smoking
options.B: Eating fresh green vegetables
options.C: Walking briskly every morning
options.D: Drinking too much clean water

explanation: Smoking harms blood vessel walls and reduces blood flow all over the body, which heavily impacts sexual function.

question: Blood type classification represents which type of measurement scale?

options.A: Nominal scale
options.B: Interval scale
options.C: Ordinal scale
options.D: Ratio scale

explanation: Nominal scales deal with named categories that do not have any mathematical order or ranking, such as blood types. [learn more](GNS224_U2_T2#GNS224_U2_T2_h2)

question: What are the two main components that make up the central nervous system?

options.A: Sensory receptors and motor organs
options.B: Nerves and ganglia
options.C: Sympathetic and parasympathetic systems
options.D: Brain and spinal cord

explanation: The central nervous system consists exclusively of the brain and the spinal cord, which serve as the primary processing center for the body. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T4#GNS211_U3_T4_h1)

question: Why must blood cultures be drawn BEFORE starting antibiotics in a suspected heart infection?

options.A: To prevent antibiotics from killing the bacteria in the sample and masking the diagnosis
options.B: To make sure the patient's blood pressure remains stable during the blood draw
options.C: To allow the white blood cell count time to normalize naturally
options.D: To ensure the laboratory technician is available to process the blood immediately

explanation: If we give antibiotics first, they might kill the germs in our lab sample, leaving us guessing about what infection we are fighting!

question: Why does community health nursing focus so much on wellness promotion compared to hospital care?

options.A: Because hospitals only treat infectious diseases rather than chronic illnesses
options.B: Because social and environmental factors heavily shape overall health outcomes
options.C: Because public health laws strictly forbid treating patients inside wards
options.D: Because individual patients refuse to visit clinics until they are very sick

explanation: You got this! When we look beyond just symptoms, we see that where people live, eat, and work plays a huge role in their health.

question: Which of these is NOT a role for a nurse doing community cancer advocacy?

options.A: Prescribing targeted chemotherapy drugs for newly diagnosed patients
options.B: Promoting clean air and smoke-free public spaces
options.C: Dispelling cultural myths about cancer transmission in local neighborhoods
options.D: Advocating for policies that provide affordable cancer screenings

explanation: Nurses rock at education and community advocacy, but prescribing medications is reserved for doctors and specialized nurse practitioners.

question: Why is it important to investigate the root cause of a workplace accident?

options.A: To avoid paying workers' compensation claims to injured staff
options.B: To satisfy legal requirements without making actual workplace changes
options.C: To find an individual employee to blame and dismiss immediately
options.D: To prevent the same incident from happening again by fixing the underlying flaw

explanation: Finding the root cause isn't about witch-hunting; it's about fixing the system so that exact accident never happens to anyone else.

question: What color and type of container is standard for collecting used sharps in the ward?

options.A: Puncture-resistant yellow container
options.B: Transparent white polythene bag
options.C: Green cardboard carton
options.D: Open black plastic bucket

explanation: You got it! Sharps need hard, puncture-proof containers—usually yellow with biohazard signs—to keep everyone safe from needle sticks.

question: How should you position a patient right after a craniotomy surgery to help keep intracranial pressure down?

options.A: Sitting upright at a 90-degree angle
options.B: Flat on the back with feet raised high
options.C: Head elevated 30 to 45 degrees
options.D: Lying flat on the operative side

explanation: Excellent clinical thinking! Elevating the head of the bed helps blood flow smoothly out of the head (venous return), preventing fluid backup and keeping pressure low.

question: Why do standard primary health clinics often struggle to attract young people?

options.A: They charge higher fees for younger patients.
options.B: They only open during school hours.
options.C: They refuse to treat patients without a parent present.
options.D: They are usually structured for either small children or older adults.

explanation: Traditional clinics are often set up for babies (immunizations) or older adults, leaving teenagers feeling awkward and out of place. Great clinics need to feel welcoming to everyone!

question: What is the best way for a nurse manager to get staff to support financial goals?

options.A: Threaten workers with dismissal if supply costs go up by one percent
options.B: Involve frontline nurses in discussions and explain that financial health supports patient care
options.C: Keep all financial reports strictly secret from the nursing staff
options.D: Punish any nurse who asks questions about where unit funds are spent

explanation: When managers communicate openly, staff can see that managing money well actually protects the hospital's ability to help patients.

question: Why are new mothers still at risk for joint injuries in the weeks right after giving birth?

options.A: The sudden loss of body weight makes the skeleton extremely brittle.
options.B: New mothers stop using their muscles entirely while resting.
options.C: Relaxin hormone remains in the body for some time, keeping joints lax.
options.D: Breastfeeding draws all the calcium out of the arm and leg bones.

explanation: Even though delivery is done, relaxin takes several weeks to completely clear out of the bloodstream, leaving ligaments loose and vulnerable.

question: What protective layers wrap around both the brain and the spinal cord?

options.A: Meninges
options.B: Ventricles
options.C: Myelin sheaths
options.D: Synapses

explanation: The meninges are like sturdy cushion layers wrapped around your delicate central nervous system for safety. [learn more](GNS211_U3_T2#GNS211_U3_T2_h3)

question: A patient with a high fever is sweating a lot and refuses to drink water. What should you do first?

options.A: Wait until the fever completely clears up
options.B: Encourage small, frequent sips of rehydration fluids
options.C: Give water pills to control body water
options.D: Stop all fluids so they don't vomit

explanation: You got it! Fevers dry people out quickly through sweating and heavy breathing, so gentle, steady hydration is key.

question: A male relative insists on answering all health questions for an adult female patient. Which concept best explains this situation?

options.A: Genetic mutation
options.B: Power dynamics
options.C: Biological sex
options.D: Symptom etiology

explanation: Spot on! Unequal power dynamics at home often mean one person takes over and speaks for others during health visits.

question: How can untreated mental health issues like depression increase a person's risk of drug abuse?

options.A: They automatically cure physical pain and prevent addiction
options.B: They guarantee the person will never touch alcohol or drugs
options.C: They may use substances to self-medicate and numb emotional pain
options.D: They stop the brain from absorbing any psychoactive compounds

explanation: When people are hurting emotionally and lack mental health support, they sometimes turn to drugs or alcohol just to find relief.

question: What do the three classic signs of diabetes—polyuria, polydipsia, and polyphagia—actually mean?

options.A: Frequent headaches, blurred vision, and dizziness
options.B: High blood pressure, rapid heart rate, and fever
options.C: Joint pain, muscle weakness, and skin rashes
options.D: Excessive urination, excessive thirst, and excessive hunger

explanation: Just break down the medical terms: 'uria' relates to urine, 'dipsia' to thirst, and 'phagia' to eating/hunger! Remembering the Greek roots makes nursing terms so much easier.

question: When is the best time to clean and disinfect a clinical weighing scale?

options.A: Only when visibly soiled with body fluids
options.B: After every single patient use
options.C: Once every week during routine cleaning
options.D: Only at the end of the work shift

explanation: Wiping the scale after each patient prevents the spread of skin infections and germs. Excellent infection control practice!

question: Which part of the brainstem contains the main control hubs for heart rate and breathing rhythms?

options.A: Cerebellum
options.B: Medulla oblongata
options.C: Midbrain
options.D: Cerebral cortex

explanation: The medulla oblongata is like the engine room of your brain, keeping your heart beating and your lungs breathing smoothly.

question: What causes the yellowing of the skin and eyes that we call jaundice?

options.A: Low levels of bicarbonate in the small intestine
options.B: Rapid breakdown of red blood cells by the pancreas
options.C: A buildup of bilirubin due to blocked bile flow
options.D: An excess of salivary amylase in the bloodstream

explanation: When bile channels get blocked (maybe by a gallstone or liver trouble), a yellow pigment called bilirubin can't escape properly. It builds up in the body and turns the skin and eyes yellow.

question: How does yellow fever pass from one person to another?

options.A: By direct skin contact with the sweat or saliva of a carrier
options.B: By sharing eating utensils or drinking cups with an infected individual
options.C: Through the bite of an infected mosquito that previously bit a sick person
options.D: Through airborne droplets released when a patient coughs or sneezes

explanation: Spot on! Yellow fever needs a mosquito middleman—you cannot catch it just by touching or breathing near someone who is sick. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T9#GNS214_U1_T9_h2)

question: You see a colleague pouring leftover liquid antibiotics down the hospital sink. What is the right nursing response?

options.A: Help pour the remaining bottles down the drain to finish faster
options.B: Stop the colleague and explain proper pharmaceutical waste disposal
options.C: Throw the empty glass bottles into the general household trash bin
options.D: Ignore the action since liquid drugs dissolve safely in water pipes

explanation: Fantastic clinical judgment! Pouring medications down regular drains pollutes local water systems. Proper disposal protects both our patients and our environment.

question: Which mineral is especially important for growing and building white blood cells to fight infections?

options.A: Potassium
options.B: Calcium
options.C: Zinc
options.D: Sodium

explanation: You got it! Zinc plays a huge role in helping your immune cells multiply and do their job when an infection tries to take hold.

question: Why is advance notice of duty rosters important for nursing staff?

options.A: It stops patients from complaining about the food
options.B: It helps nurses plan their personal lives and reduces fatigue
options.C: It allows the hospital to buy drugs at cheaper wholesale prices
options.D: It removes the need for any night shifts on the ward

explanation: Predictable schedules allow staff to rest properly and manage family responsibilities, lowering burnout. [learn more](GST321_U1_T11#GST321_U1_T11_h5)

question: What does morbidity measure in a community?

options.A: The state of being unhealthy or diseased
options.B: The total number of registered deaths
options.C: The number of new babies born in a year
options.D: The amount of money earned by hospitals

explanation: Morbidity focuses on illness, sickness, and disease prevalence rather than death itself. [learn more](GNS313_U4_T2#GNS313_U4_T2_h4)

question: Why should a patient close their eyes during sensory testing?

options.B: To prevent them from using visual cues to guide their answers
options.C: To prevent dizziness caused by looking around the room
options.D: To help them fall asleep during a lengthy examination

explanation: Closing the eyes ensures that the patient is genuinely feeling the stimulus rather than just watching where you touch. [learn more](GNS221_U2_T1#GNS221_U2_T1_h6)

question: What is the primary purpose of establishing a referral pathway for home delivery?

options.A: Complying with hospital decoration rules
options.B: Reducing the cost of antenatal drugs
options.C: Ensuring fast transfer to a hospital if complications occur
options.D: Giving the nurse time to rest during labor

explanation: A referral pathway guarantees that the patient can be moved smoothly to a higher level of care without unnecessary delay. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T9#GNS225_U3_T9_h7)

question: A patient has a hard mass of stool stuck in the rectum (impaction), yet they keep passing small amounts of liquid. Why does this happen?

options.A: Infection has completely liquefied the entire colon
options.B: Liquid stool leaks around the solid blocked mass
options.C: The small intestine is hyperactive and rushing food
options.D: The kidneys are producing excessive fluid waste

explanation: Don't let this trick you in the ward! Liquid waste from higher up in the gut finds a way to slip past the hard, blocked stool, which can easily look like normal diarrhea.

question: How does severe body cooling (hypothermia) directly harm a bleeding patient?

options.A: It speeds up platelet production too fast
options.B: It causes blood vessels to clamp shut permanently
options.C: It prevents kidneys from producing acidic urine
options.D: It slows down the chemical reactions needed for blood to clot

explanation: Clotting enzymes are like workers in a factory—when the patient gets too cold, those workers slow down and can't get the job done!

question: What is the primary difference between hearing and active listening?

options.A: Active listening only happens during telephone conversations
options.B: Hearing requires the nurse to take detailed written notes
options.C: Active listening requires full concentration and understanding
options.D: Hearing is a deliberate skill that takes years to learn

explanation: Hearing is just the physical detection of sound, whereas active listening is a conscious mental effort to comprehend the speaker's message and feelings. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T22#GNS225_U2_T22_h4)

question: You notice a red patch over a patient's lower back that does not turn white when you press it with your finger. What does this usually mean?

options.A: A normal reaction to sleeping on cotton sheets
options.B: An early stage pressure injury starting to form
options.C: A healing bruise from a previous minor fall
options.D: An allergic reaction to bath soap

explanation: Great catch! When skin stays red and doesn't blanch (turn white) under pressure, it's a key early warning sign that deep tissue is suffering from a lack of blood flow.

question: Which blood tests are most important to check before a paracentesis to prevent bleeding?

options.A: Serum creatinine and BUN
options.B: Fasting blood glucose level
options.C: Coagulation profile and platelets
options.D: Total white blood cell count

explanation: We always check clotting times and platelets first to make sure the patient won't bleed too much from the needle poke.

question: A nurse notices that a postoperative surgical wound is increasingly red, warm, and draining foul-smelling pus. What is the most appropriate immediate action?

options.A: Wait until the patient's scheduled discharge day to mention it
options.B: Assume this is a normal healing process and take no action
options.C: Report the findings and document them clearly for the care team
options.D: Apply a dry bandage and advise the patient not to look at it

explanation: Prompt reporting and documentation ensure the medical team can investigate and treat a potential surgical site infection early. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h9)

question: What is a key action Nigerian nurses can take to promote male involvement?

options.A: Send police officers to bring absent fathers to the hospital
options.B: Ignore fathers in the waiting room to focus only on mothers
options.C: Actively invite men into consultation rooms and address both parents
options.D: Charge men extra fees for entering maternal health clinics

explanation: Nurses promote involvement by making fathers feel welcome and included in health discussions right from the start. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T58#GNS214_U1_T58_h7)

question: A patient with severe knee osteoarthritis gets no relief from oral pain relievers and physical therapy. What intervention is a nurse most likely to prepare the patient for next?

options.A: A complete blood transfusion
options.B: An intraarticular joint injection
options.C: Intravenous antibiotic therapy
options.D: An intramuscular vaccine dose

explanation: When conservative oral treatments fail for localized joint wear, doctors often step up to direct joint injections. [learn more](GNS125_U3_T9#GNS125_U3_T9_h3)

question: Why is it super important for nurses to know the generic name of a drug?

options.A: It is the only name recognized by hospital billing departments
options.B: It remains universal and prevents confusion across different manufacturing companies
options.C: It tells the nurse the exact physical shape and color of the pill
options.D: It automatically guarantees the drug is more affordable for the patient

explanation: You nailed it. Generic names stay the same everywhere, saving us from company name confusion!

question: Which route for measuring body temperature is generally considered the most accurate reflection of core temperature?

options.A: Tympanic
options.B: Rectal
options.C: Oral
options.D: Axillary

explanation: Rectal measurements closely approximate core body temperature because the site is protected from external environmental influences. [learn more](GNS221_U3_T3#GNS221_U3_T3_h3)

question: How does early Pick's disease usually look different from Alzheimer's disease?

options.A: Alzheimer's disease exclusively affects people under age fifty.
options.B: Alzheimer's disease causes rapid physical paralysis unlike Pick's disease.
options.C: Pick's disease alters behavior and personality first rather than memory.
options.D: Pick's disease begins with severe visual hallucinations.

explanation: You've got this! While Alzheimer's usually attacks memory first, Pick's disease changes how a person acts, talks to others, and handles their emotions right from the start.

question: Why should evaluation be participatory in community health projects?

options.A: it prevents the government from auditing the health center
options.B: It allows locals to assess their own progress and build capacity
options.C: It guarantees that no future health problems will occur
options.D: It ensures that nurses avoid blame if the project fails

explanation: Involving the community in evaluation builds local analytical skills and ensures true ownership of the project's outcomes. [learn more](GNS124_U4_T5#GNS124_U4_T5_h8)

question: What's the main difference between a regular fever and hyperthermia?

options.A: Hyperthermia responds to antipyretic drugs, while fever never does.
options.B: Fever only occurs in children, while hyperthermia only occurs in adults.
options.C: Fever involves the brain raising its temperature target, while hyperthermia is a failure to cool down.
options.D: Hyperthermia is caused by infections, while fever is caused by weather.

explanation: Think of it this way: a fever happens because your brain's thermostat is intentionally turned up (like fighting an infection). Hyperthermia happens when the body is overwhelmed by heat and can't cool itself down, and normal fever meds won't fix that thermostat setting!

question: What is the clinical term for when blood escapes from the blood vessels?

options.A: Hemostasis
options.B: Haemorrhage
options.C: Hypovolemia
options.D: Hemolysis

explanation: Haemorrhage is simply the medical word for bleeding. You've got this! Think of it as blood escaping its normal highway.

question: Which of the following is NOT a reason why nurses must follow strict infection control during an epidemic?

options.A: To prevent the nurse from contracting the infectious agent
options.B: To protect other vulnerable patients admitted to the ward
options.C: To stop the hospital environment from spreading the disease
options.D: To guarantee that patients pay their hospital bills on time

explanation: Brilliant! Infection control is entirely about safety and stopping the spread of germs, and has nothing to do with hospital bills or payments.

question: How do screen-readers and talking appliances primarily help a visually impaired patient?

options.A: By physically guiding the patient's hands across household objects
options.B: By curing the underlying disease causing progressive blindness
options.C: By translating digital text and operational cues into audio feedback
options.D: By directly improving the optical clarity of damaged retinal tissues

explanation: Technology is amazing! When eyes need a break or can't see, turning text and appliance settings into spoken audio lets patients stay independent and in control.

question: What causes the glandular tissue of the breast to shrink after menopause?

options.A: Increased activity of Montgomery glands
options.B: Thickening of Cooper's ligaments
options.C: Declining estrogen levels
options.D: Blockage of the lactiferous ducts

explanation: When estrogen levels drop after menopause, glandular tissue regresses and is largely replaced by fat. [learn more](GNS121_U5_T16#GNS121_U5_T16_h7)

question: What is the safest way to unplug a machine from the wall socket on the ward?

options.A: Grip the molded plug firmly and pull straight out
options.B: Pull the device across the room until it unplugs
options.C: Yank the flexible cord until the plug pops loose
options.D: Switch off the main circuit breaker for the ward

explanation: Always hold the solid plug itself! Pulling by the cord damages the internal wires and can cause a nasty spark.

question: What emergency procedure is used to drain extra fluid from around the heart during cardiac tamponade?

options.A: Thoracentesis
options.B: Cardioversion
options.C: Pericardiocentesis
options.D: Paracentesis

explanation: Pericardiocentesis involves gently passing a needle into the pericardial sac to draw out fluid and relieve dangerous pressure on the heart. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h7)

question: A patient with depression frequently wakes up at 3:00 AM and cannot fall back asleep. What pattern is this?

options.A: Sleep-onset insomnia
options.B: Sleep apnea overlap
options.C: Circadian phase delay
options.D: Early morning awakening

explanation: Waking up way too early and failing to get back to sleep is known as early morning awakening (or terminal insomnia), which is frequently seen in people dealing with depression.

question: How do nitrate medications help stop chest pain?

options.A: By speeding up the electrical rhythm of the heart
options.B: By dilating blood vessels to reduce heart workload
options.C: By thickening the blood to improve clot formation
options.D: By increasing the heart rate to pump faster

explanation: Nitrates act like widening the road—they relax blood vessels so blood flows more easily, taking a huge load off the heart and easing the pain.

question: What is the very first thing you should do when someone asks you a drug-related question?

options.A: Consulting a tertiary drug reference textbook
options.B: Formulating the final verbal response for the doctor
options.C: Searching the primary medical literature for clinical trials
options.D: Securing demographic and background data about the patient and requester

explanation: Spot on! Before you can hunt for an answer, you need to know who is asking and the patient's specific health situation.

question: Which of these is a classic sign of postpartum endometritis (infection of the uterus lining)?

options.A: Sudden weight gain and facial swelling
options.B: Foul-smelling lochia and fever
options.C: High blood pressure and visual changes
options.D: Painful urination and flank pain

explanation: When the uterine lining gets infected, it usually lets you know through fever, tenderness, and vaginal discharge that smells unusual or foul. You're building great clinical instincts! [learn more](GNS226_U3_T016#GNS226_U3_T016_h5)

question: Which symptom is a common physical sign of high stress?

options.A: Complete paralysis of the limbs
options.B: Uncontrollable tremors in the legs
options.C: Muscle tension and headaches
options.D: Joint swelling and redness

explanation: When stressed, we often clench our muscles without realizing it, which frequently leads to tight shoulders, sore muscles, and tension headaches.

question: What is the most common and immediate cause of death after an unsafe abortion?

options.A: Hemorrhage
options.B: Uterine cancer
options.C: Renal failure
options.D: Gestational diabetes

explanation: Heavy, uncontrolled bleeding is the number one emergency here. When tissues are torn or left behind in unsterile procedures, severe bleeding can turn fatal very quickly if we don't act fast.

question: Why does primary health care place heavy emphasis on nutrition and safe water alongside medical treatment?

options.A: Nurses are trained as civil engineers rather than clinicians
options.B: Preventing disease through basic sanitation stops sickness before it starts
options.C: Doctors refuse to treat patients who do not drink boiled water
options.D: Water and food are more profitable than pharmaceutical drugs

explanation: Clean water and good nutrition address the root environmental causes of infection, reducing the burden on clinics. [learn more](GNS124_U1_T5#GNS124_U1_T5_h7)

question: Why is having a clear 'case definition' so important during a disease outbreak?

options.A: It guarantees that the disease will not spread to neighboring towns.
options.B: It automatically cures the patients who fit the diagnostic description.
options.C: It prevents the government from spending money on laboratory testing.
options.D: It ensures all investigators identify and count cases using the exact same criteria.

explanation: Spot on! A clear case definition makes sure every nurse and doctor is looking for the exact same signs, preventing confusion in our records.

question: As a midwife checking the lower boundary of the pelvic cavity, which bones help form the pelvic outlet?

options.A: Acetabulum and pubic tubercle
options.B: Ischial tuberosities and coccyx
options.C: Linea terminalis and sacral ala
options.D: Iliac crests and sacral promontory

explanation: Think of the bottom exit of the pelvis: it's bounded by your tailbone (coccyx), the sitting bones (ischial tuberosities), and the front pubic bone.

question: A woman who delivered a healthy baby six hours ago starts bleeding heavily, and her uterus feels soft and boggy. What should the nurse do first?

options.A: Wait for two hours to see if the bleeding stops on its own
options.B: Leave the ward to call the senior consultant doctor immediately
options.C: Encourage the mother to stand up and walk around the room
options.D: Massage the uterus gently to stimulate contraction and expel clots

explanation: A soft, boggy uterus after delivery indicates uterine atony, which requires immediate fundal massage to stimulate contraction and reduce bleeding. [learn more](GNS216_U1_T7#GNS216_U1_T7_h4)

question: What must be obtained before starting data collection with human participants in a study?

options.A: A commercial sponsor
options.B: Surgical clearance
options.C: A patent for a new drug
options.D: Ethical approval

explanation: Patient safety and rights always come first. Ethical approval ensures your study is safe and respects human dignity. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: How does expressive aphasia usually show up in a stroke patient?

options.A: Severe shaking of the hands during writing
options.B: Inability to hear sound waves entering the ear
options.C: Total blindness in both visual fields
options.D: Difficulty speaking or finding the right words to say

explanation: With expressive aphasia, the patient usually understands what you're saying, but struggles to get their own words out. Patience is key!

question: A nursing student is asked to run a school mental health drama club. What is the main benefit of using drama for teenagers?

options.A: It guarantees that none of the students will ever feel sad
options.B: It tests their ability to memorize medical textbooks word for word
options.C: It replaces the need for professional psychiatric nurses
options.D: It entertains them while teaching healthy ways to cope with emotional stress

explanation: Creative methods like drama engage young minds effectively, making sensitive health messages relatable and easy to remember. [learn more](GNS314_U4_T7#GNS314_U4_T7_h7)

question: What finding in a pregnant patient's urine points to prolonged vomiting and starvation?

options.A: Ketones
options.B: Red blood cells
options.C: Glucose
options.D: Bilirubin

explanation: When the body can't keep food down, it starts burning its own fat for fuel. This breakdown leaves behind ketones in the urine—a classic sign of prolonged vomiting!

question: Why does the pregnant body develop natural insulin resistance in the later stages of gestation?

options.A: To speed up the digestion of dietary fats and proteins
options.B: To keep more glucose circulating in the blood for fetal uptake
options.C: To help the pancreas rest from producing digestive enzymes
options.D: To prevent the mother from ever developing type 2 diabetes

explanation: Insulin resistance ensures that less glucose is used by maternal tissues, making more available in the bloodstream to cross the placenta for the baby. [learn more](GNS226_U2_T003#GNS226_U2_T003_h4)

question: Why is active severe diarrhea a major drawback for using rectal suppositories?

options.A: It causes the suppository to dissolve instantly into gas

question: What is the primary purpose of problem identification in community health?

options.A: To close down traditional healing centers in the community

options.C: To write medical prescriptions for every household in the ward
options.D: To discover and define health gaps within a target population

explanation: Problem identification focuses on finding and describing unmet health needs so they can be addressed. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T17#GNS225_U2_T17_h2)

question: What exactly is Sheehan's syndrome?

options.A: Immune system attack on the adrenal glands brought on by stress
options.B: Death of pituitary tissue due to severe blood loss right after childbirth
options.C: A benign tumor causing sudden vision loss in older men
options.D: A genetic inability to make antidiuretic hormone after bumping your head

explanation: During delivery, a massive hemorrhage can drop blood pressure so low that the hardworking pituitary gland is starved of blood and oxygen, leading to tissue death (necrosis).

question: A patient recovering from defibulation surgery is in the ward. What is a key nursing priority?

options.B: Applying tight pressure dressings to keep edges closed
options.C: Providing meticulous wound care to prevent new adhesion formation
options.D: Encouraging immediate heavy exercise to build strength
